title: Breaking Bad

title: Ozark
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Cliffhanger-driven crime escalation across four complete seasons, engineered for continuation. title: Person of Interest

High sustain once there, but a long low-hook runway — a bigger ask than Dark's slow start.

title: Succession

title: Task
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Mare of Easttown's creator running a manhunt engine, which is inherently propulsive, across a short first season. Critics call it 'unrelentingly bleak but riveting' — the bleakness is what holds it at 4 rather than Mare's 5.

title: The Expanse
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Serialised protomolecule arc with real payoffs across a complete run — the Foundation/Silo cluster where you scored 5. Docked one for the dense faction politics in early episodes, which take a while to become legible and slow the hook.

title: True Detective
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: S1's dual-timeline investigation is a strong mystery engine with mounting dread. The philosophical monologues and deliberate Louisiana languor slow it below a pure page-turner, and the anthology format means momentum resets after eight episodes.

title: We Were the Lucky Ones
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: WWII family-survival story cross-cutting between separated siblings, which builds natural 'what happened to them' momentum. Heavy subject matter caps consecutive viewing — the same ceiling as your other WWII together watches rather than a soap-tier 5.

title: 12 Monkeys
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Time-loop plotting is a payoff machine with twisty episode-end hooks across four complete seasons — structurally very bingeable. Mid-budget execution and occasional expository filler keep it off 5.

title: Arcane
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Nine episodes in three-episode acts, each ending on a deliberate escalation, and short enough to clear quickly. Held at 4 because the no-franchise-hook problem is an engagement risk for you specifically — your animated wins are all IP-driven.

title: Black Doves
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 5/5: Six-episode spy thriller with a ticking-clock Christmas setting and constant reversals. Slow Horses is your binge 5 in exactly this lane, and short-run British spy is the most reliably compulsive shape in your together data.

title: Boardwalk Empire
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Stately Sopranos-lineage period crime — lavish and slow, built on political manoeuvring rather than cliffhangers, across five seasons. This is the prestige-heavy class where your own scores cluster at 3 (Better Call Saul, Boardwalk's closest tonal relative).

title: Bodies
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 5/5: Eight-episode limited series, one murder across four eras, structured so each timeline cuts away on a hook. title: Counterpart
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Tight two-season spy mystery with a doppelganger conceit that generates constant reveals. Cold, deliberate direction and a cancelled ending hold it just below 5, but the episode count is small enough to clear fast.

title: Devs
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Only eight episodes, but deliberately hypnotic and slow — its own prediction already carries a slow-burn/experimental penalty and a style-over-substance risk. Garland prioritises mood over momentum, so it watches in ones rather than runs.

title: Dexter
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Case engine plus a season-long antagonist arc (Trinity being the high point) makes it genuinely propulsive — this is the serialised-spine shape, not pure case-of-the-week. Eight seasons and a well-known late decline stop it short of 5.

title: Down Cemetery Road
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Short-run Mick Herron conspiracy mystery — a missing-child hook is strong pull, and Herron plots move. Audience score notably below critics (59 vs 79) suggests some pacing drag, so 4 rather than Slow Horses' 5.

title: Drops of God
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: A tasting-competition structure gives every episode a built-in challenge-and-result beat, which is reliable episodic momentum. Subtitles across French and Japanese and a contemplative register keep it off 5.

predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Eight episodes, but the back half turns into an investigative inquiry after the hurricane crisis resolves, which drains urgency. Harrowing medical-triage content makes consecutive episodes hard going — high purpose, low compulsion.

title: FROM
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 5/5: Mystery-box horror that ends nearly every episode on a cliffhanger and withholds answers by design — its own prediction calls it addictive. title: Half Man

title: House of the Dragon
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Game of Thrones political intrigue with strong episode-end escalations and a civil war building. Held at 4 by the multi-year time jumps and recasting in S1, which repeatedly reset investment and interrupted momentum.

title: Line of Duty

title: Ludwig

title: Maid

title: Manhunt
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: A manhunt is an inherently propulsive spine, and each anthology season runs only ~8 episodes, so commitment is low. Period true-crime pacing is more measured than a thriller, so 4 rather than 5.

title: Operation Buffalo
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Short Australian period limited series, but its tonal mix of nuclear-testing satire and drama is uneven, and the pacing is discursive rather than driving. Steady watching, no strong pull to the next episode.

predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 5/5: Clone-conspiracy thriller that runs on reveals and end-of-episode cliffhangers, with a propulsive first two seasons in particular. Sits squarely in your compulsive solo sci-fi lane alongside Stranger Things and Silo, both scored 5.

title: Peaky Blinders
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Tight six-episode seasons with a clear antagonist arc each series, so momentum is high and commitment per season is low. Stylised, occasionally repetitive plotting across six seasons keeps it below 5.

title: Somebody Somewhere
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Quiet half-hour character piece about grief and friendship with almost no plot momentum — critically adored for exactly that. Short seasons make it easy, but nothing compels the next episode.

predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Non-linear literary structure that jumps across twenty years, and its own prediction notes it is thoughtful rather than action-focused. The payoff is cumulative and genuinely moving, but the hook is weak — a slow-burn to commit to, not race through.
